--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [ConformanceReport]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: The results of a CDISC conformance check. twitter-card: title: >- [ConformanceReport]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: The results of a CDISC conformance check. title: >- [ConformanceReport]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: The results of a CDISC conformance check. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The results of a CDISC conformance check. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_submission.py#L1336-L2967){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature ConformanceReport( validations=dict(), package=None, agency=None, core=None, native_result=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A `ConformanceReport` holds the results of checking a set of CDISC datasets for conformance to their standard. It is returned by [`validate_sdtmig()`](`pointblank.validate_sdtmig`), [`validate_cdisc_submission()`](`pointblank.validate_cdisc_submission`) and the `SubmissionPackage` method [`validate_conformance()`](`pointblank.SubmissionPackage.validate_conformance`), and is rarely made directly. The report has one of three forms, depending on the engine that did the checks: - **Built-in rules** ([`is_rules`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.is_rules`) is `True`): the results of Pointblank's bundled catalog of SDTMIG rules. Each rule has a status of `"pass"`, `"fail"`, `"error"` (the rule couldn't be evaluated), `"not_applicable"` (an input that it needs, such as a Define-XML, wasn't given) or `"not_supported"`. The rules that check values give the failing records, which are in [`findings_df()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.findings_df`) and [`get_findings_table()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.get_findings_table`). - **CDISC CORE** ([`is_core`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.is_core`) is `True`): the results of the CDISC CORE engine, with CORE's own rule statuses (such as `"SUCCESS"`, `"ISSUE REPORTED"` and `"SKIPPED"`). A report of this form can also be made from a saved CORE report with [`from_core_report()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.from_core_report`). - **Validate-based**: a [`Validate`](`pointblank.Validate`) validation for each dataset, from `SubmissionPackage.validate_conformance(engine="validate")`. Each validation can be had with [`get_validation()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.get_validation`). The methods [`summary()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.summary`), [`issues()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.issues`) and [`all_passed()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.all_passed`) work for all three forms. In a notebook, a report of the built-in rules is shown as the table of [`get_tabular_report()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.get_tabular_report`). A CORE report is shown as a short summary with a table of its issues, and a Validate-based report as the validation report of each dataset. Printing a report of any form gives a text summary. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [validations]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, Validate]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [dict()]{.doc-parameter-default} : The validation for each dataset, keyed by dataset name, for a Validate-based report. The default is an empty dict. [package]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [SubmissionPackage | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The [`SubmissionPackage`](`pointblank.SubmissionPackage`) that was checked. The default is `None`. [agency]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The regulatory agency, such as `"FDA"`, which is only used as a label in the report. The default is `None`. [core]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [ParsedCoreReport | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : CORE's results, for a CDISC CORE report. The default is `None`. [native_result]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NativeConformanceResult | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The results of the rules, for a report of the built-in rules. The default is `None`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a small DM dataset with the built-in rules. It has a date that isn't in the ISO 8601 format, a negative age and a `SEX` value that isn't in its codelist: ::: {#21d84f79 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame( { "STUDYID": ["STUDY01"] * 3, "DOMAIN": ["DM"] * 3, "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001", "STUDY01-002", "STUDY01-003"], "RFSTDTC": ["2024-01-15", "15JAN2024", "2024-01-17"], "AGE": [34, 51, -38], "SEX": ["M", "F", "FEMALE"], } ) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm}) print(report) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ConformanceReport (Built-in Rules) sdtmig 3-4 362 rules (fail=10, not_applicable=12, pass=340) 10 issues — FAIL ``` ::: ::: Ten of the 362 rules fail. Most of them are about what the dataset lacks, such as the DM variables `SUBJID` and `RACE` and the TS and TA datasets. The failing records are found by three of the rules: ::: {#076bf2de .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} report.findings_df().select("rule_id", "row_index", "checked_column", "checked_value") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

To see the results of all the rules as a table, use [`get_tabular_report()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.get_tabular_report`). ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~validate_sdtmig`) : Check SDTM datasets with the built-in rules. [](`~validate_cdisc_submission`) : Check a folder of datasets with CDISC CORE. [](`~SubmissionPackage`) : A set of datasets to check together. ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [n_datasets](#n_datasets){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | The number of datasets that were checked. | | [is_core](#is_core){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Whether the report holds the results of CDISC CORE. | | [is_rules](#is_rules){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Whether the report holds the results of Pointblank's built-in rules. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [n_datasets]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The number of datasets that were checked. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [n_datasets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} For a report of the built-in rules, this is the number of datasets that were given, and for a Validate-based report, the number of validations. For a CDISC CORE report, it is the number of datasets in CORE's `Dataset_Details`. Datasets that a rule requires but that are missing (such as TS) aren't counted. This is a property, so it's used without parentheses. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a package of two datasets with the built-in rules: ::: {#2c959e87 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame({"STUDYID": ["STUDY01"], "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001"]}) ae = pl.DataFrame({"STUDYID": ["STUDY01"], "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001"], "AESEQ": [1]}) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm, "AE": ae}) report.n_datasets ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: The two datasets were checked, though some rules are about the TS and TA datasets, which the package doesn't have. ### [is_core]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the report holds the results of CDISC CORE. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [is_core]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is `True` for the report of [`validate_cdisc_submission()`](`pointblank.validate_cdisc_submission`), of `SubmissionPackage.validate_conformance(engine="core")` and of [`from_core_report()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.from_core_report`). Some methods only work for one form of report, so this tells code which form it has. This is a property, so it's used without parentheses. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a DM dataset with the built-in rules and look at the form of the report: ::: {#2b0fb54d .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame({"STUDYID": ["STUDY01"], "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001"], "SEX": ["F"]}) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm}) print(report.is_core, report.is_rules) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` False True ``` ::: ::: The report is of the built-in rules, so `is_core` is `False` and [`is_rules`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.is_rules`) is `True`. ### [is_rules]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the report holds the results of Pointblank's built-in rules. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [is_rules]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is `True` for the report of [`validate_sdtmig()`](`pointblank.validate_sdtmig`) and of `SubmissionPackage.validate_conformance()` with its default engine (when the package's standard has a bundled rules catalog). Only these reports have [`findings_df()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.findings_df`), [`get_findings_table()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.get_findings_table`) and [`get_tabular_report()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.get_tabular_report`). This is a property, so it's used without parentheses. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a package with each of the two Pointblank engines: ::: {#a3d2d96b .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame({"STUDYID": ["STUDY01"], "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001"], "SEX": ["F"]}) study = pb.SubmissionPackage(datasets={"DM": dm}) print(study.validate_conformance().is_rules) print(study.validate_conformance(engine="validate").is_rules) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` True False ``` ::: ::: The `"validate"` engine gives a report of [`Validate`](`pointblank.Validate`) validations, so its `is_rules` is `False`, as is its [`is_core`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.is_core`). ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | datasets conform, with nothing failing. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_submission.py#L1608-L1649){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature all_passed() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This gives a single answer for a conformance check, as is needed in a script or a pipeline that should stop when the data don't conform. What counts as passing depends on the form of the report: - For the built-in rules, no rule has the status `"fail"`. A failing rule of `"Warning"` sensitivity counts too. Rules that are not applicable or couldn't be evaluated don't. - For CDISC CORE, no rule reported an issue or an execution error. - For a Validate-based report, every step of every validation passed (with no failing test units). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if nothing failed, otherwise `False`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a DM dataset with the built-in rules: ::: {#ef7cd034 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame({"STUDYID": ["STUDY01"], "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001"], "SEX": ["F"]}) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm}) report.all_passed() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` False ``` ::: ::: The dataset lacks many of the variables that DM requires, and the TS and TA datasets are missing, so some rules fail. The rules that fail can be listed with [`rules()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.rules`), as in `report.rules(status="fail")`. ### [summary()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Summarize the results of the conformance check as a dict. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_submission.py#L1722-L1813){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature summary() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The summary has the counts that are shown when a report is printed, in a form that code can use, such as for logging the results of a run or for comparing two runs. Its keys depend on the form of the report. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : For a report of the built-in rules, a dict with the keys `standard`, `version`, `engine` (which is `"built-in"`), `ct_packages` (the controlled terminology packages that were used), `n_rules`, `status_counts` (the number of rules with each status), `n_issues` (the total number of issues) and `all_passed`. For a CDISC CORE report, a dict with the keys `standard`, `version`, `engine_version` (the version of CORE), `engine` (which is `"core"`), `n_rules`, `status_counts`, `n_issues`, `n_datasets` and `all_passed`. For a Validate-based report, a dict with an entry for each dataset. Each entry is a dict with the keys `n_steps`, `n_steps_failed`, `n_failed` (the number of failing test units) and `all_passed`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a small DM dataset with the built-in rules and summarize the results: ::: {#78e91737 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame( { "STUDYID": ["STUDY01"] * 3, "DOMAIN": ["DM"] * 3, "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001", "STUDY01-002", "STUDY01-003"], "RFSTDTC": ["2024-01-15", "15JAN2024", "2024-01-17"], "AGE": [34, 51, -38], "SEX": ["M", "F", "FEMALE"], } ) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm}) report.summary() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` {'standard': 'sdtmig', 'version': '3-4', 'engine': 'built-in', 'ct_packages': ['sdtm-ct-2024-09-27'], 'n_rules': 362, 'status_counts': {'pass': 340, 'fail': 10, 'not_applicable': 12}, 'n_issues': 10, 'all_passed': False} ``` ::: ::: The version is given as `"3-4"`, the form that the rules catalog uses. The issue count is the sum of the issues of all the rules: each failing record counts for a rule that checks values, and a failing rule counts once for a rule that checks the presence of variables or datasets. ### [get_tabular_report()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Make a table of the results of the built-in rules. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_submission.py#L2659-L2885){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature get_tabular_report() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The table has a row for each rule in the catalog, so it shows at a glance which rules failed and how many issues each one found. It is how a report of the built-in rules is shown in a notebook. For the failing records themselves, use [`get_findings_table()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.get_findings_table`) or [`findings_df()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.findings_df`). Each row has a colored bar for its status (green for a pass, red for a failure, amber for an error and gray for a rule that is not applicable or not supported), the rule's identifier, its domain, its type (such as `Record` for a check of values or `Variable` for a check that variables are present), its number of issues and its description. The failing rules come first, then the rules with errors, the passing rules and the rules that are not applicable or not supported. The title has a `PASS` or `FAIL` badge, and the subtitle has the standard and its version, the agency (if one was given) and the number of rules with each status. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [GT]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The table, as a [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/) `GT` object. ::: #### Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the report isn't of the built-in rules. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a small DM dataset with the built-in rules and make the table: ::: {#d4c9a65d .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame( { "STUDYID": ["STUDY01"] * 3, "DOMAIN": ["DM"] * 3, "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001", "STUDY01-002", "STUDY01-003"], "RFSTDTC": ["2024-01-15", "15JAN2024", "2024-01-17"], "AGE": [34, 51, -38], "SEX": ["M", "F", "FEMALE"], } ) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm}) report.get_tabular_report() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}

For the built-in rules, this can be `"pass"`, `"fail"`, `"error"`, `"not_applicable"` or `"not_supported"`. Each issue is a dict, whose keys depend on the form of the report. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [severity]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : For a Validate-based report, only keep the issues of this severity: `"warning"`, `"error"` or `"critical"`. This is ignored for the other forms of report. The default is `None`, which keeps all the issues. [status]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : For a CDISC CORE report, only keep the issues of rules with this status, such as `"ISSUE REPORTED"`. This is ignored for the other forms of report. As a DataFrame, the findings are easy to filter by rule, count by subject, save as a CSV file, or join back to the datasets to look at the records in full. The rules that check values (record checks, dataset contents checks and checks against the Define-XML's codelists) give findings. Rules that check whether variables or datasets are present have a number of issues but no findings. Directories in the path that don't exist are created. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Path]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The path of the file that was written. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a small DM dataset with the built-in rules and save the report in a temporary directory: ::: {#d53fc6b0 .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} import json import tempfile from pathlib import Path import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame( { "STUDYID": ["STUDY01"] * 3, "DOMAIN": ["DM"] * 3, "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001", "STUDY01-002", "STUDY01-003"], "SEX": ["M", "F", "FEMALE"], } ) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm}) path = report.to_json(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "conformance" / "dm.json") saved = json.loads(path.read_text()) print(saved["summary"]["status_counts"]) print(saved["issues"][0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` {'pass': 342, 'fail': 8, 'not_applicable': 12} {'dataset': 'DM', 'rule_id': 'SDTM-007', 'rule_type': 'RECORD_CHECK', 'message': 'SEX value is not in the SEX codelist.', 'n_issues': 1, 'sensitivity': 'Error', 'status': 'fail'} ``` ::: ::: The `conformance` directory didn't exist, so it was created. Each issue is saved with all its keys, as `issues()` gives it. ### [to_excel()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Save the report as an Excel workbook. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_submission.py#L2210-L2381){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature to_excel(path) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A workbook is a convenient way to share the results of a conformance check with people who review them in a spreadsheet. The sheets depend on the form of the report: - For the built-in rules, `Rules_Report` has a row for each rule, with its type, dataset, status, sensitivity, number of issues and message. `Issues` has the rules with issues (as from [`issues()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.issues`)), and `Summary` has the entries of [`summary()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.summary`). - For CDISC CORE, the sheets are `Issue_Summary`, `Issue_Details`, `Rules_Report` and `Conformance_Details`, like those of CORE's own Excel report. - For a Validate-based report, `Issues` has the failing steps and `Summary` has a row for each dataset. A sheet that would be empty, such as `Issues` when there are no issues, is left out. The `openpyxl` and `pandas` packages are needed for writing the workbook. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [path]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Path]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The path of the file to write, including its name (which usually ends in `.xlsx`). Directories in the path that don't exist are created. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Path]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The path of the file that was written. ::: #### Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ImportError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `openpyxl` or `pandas` isn't installed. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a small DM dataset with the built-in rules and save the report in a temporary directory: ::: {#96e94d8b .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} import tempfile from pathlib import Path import pandas as pd import pointblank as pb import polars as pl dm = pl.DataFrame( { "STUDYID": ["STUDY01"] * 3, "DOMAIN": ["DM"] * 3, "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001", "STUDY01-002", "STUDY01-003"], "SEX": ["M", "F", "FEMALE"], } ) report = pb.validate_sdtmig({"DM": dm}) path = report.to_excel(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "dm_conformance.xlsx") pd.ExcelFile(path).sheet_names ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=19} ``` ['Rules_Report', 'Issues', 'Summary'] ``` ::: ::: Here's the start of the `Rules_Report` sheet, whose rows are in the order of the rules catalog: ::: {#1c6815b9 .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name="Rules_Report").head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ```{=html}
Rule ID Rule Type Dataset Status Sensitivity Issues Message
0 SDTM-001 DOMAIN_PRESENCE_CHECK DM pass Error 0 DM (Demographics) domain is required in every ...
1 SDTM-002 RECORD_CHECK DM pass Error 0 STUDYID must not be null in any domain.
2 SDTM-003 RECORD_CHECK DM pass Error 0 DOMAIN must not be null in any SDTM dataset.
``` ::: ::: The workbook has a row for each of the 362 rules, so the passing rules are recorded as well as the failing ones. ### [from_core_report()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Make a report from the JSON report of a CDISC CORE run. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_submission.py#L1439-L1542){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature from_core_report( report, package=None, agency=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} CDISC CORE can be run on its own (as `core validate ... -of JSON`), and its JSON report can be kept for later. The `from_core_report()` class method reads such a report into a `ConformanceReport`, which gives it the same methods as the report of [`validate_cdisc_submission()`](`pointblank.validate_cdisc_submission`). The JSON report has five sections: `Conformance_Details` (the standard, its version and the version of CORE), `Dataset_Details`, `Issue_Summary` (the number of issues for each rule and dataset), `Issue_Details` (one entry for each failing record) and `Rules_Report` (the status of each rule). A file written by [`to_json()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.to_json`) from a CORE report has the same sections, so it can be read back with this method. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [report]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict | ParsedCoreReport]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The CORE report, as a dict (such as from `json.load()`) or as the already parsed report of an earlier `ConformanceReport` (its `core` attribute). [package]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [SubmissionPackage | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The [`SubmissionPackage`](`pointblank.SubmissionPackage`) that CORE checked. The default is `None`. [agency]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The regulatory agency, such as `"FDA"`, which is only used as a label in the report. The default is `None`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ConformanceReport]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A report of CORE's results, whose [`is_core`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.is_core`) is `True`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's write a short report by hand in CORE's format, for three rules on a DM and an AE dataset. One rule found an AE record whose subject isn't in DM, one rule passed and one was skipped: ::: {#5139690c .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb core_json = { "Conformance_Details": { "CORE_Engine_Version": "0.16.0", "Standard": "SDTMIG", "Version": "V3.4", }, "Dataset_Details": [ {"filename": "dm.xpt", "label": "Demographics", "length": 3}, {"filename": "ae.xpt", "label": "Adverse Events", "length": 2}, ], "Issue_Summary": [ { "dataset": "ae.xpt", "core_id": "CORE-000201", "message": "USUBJID is not found in DM.USUBJID", "issues": 1, } ], "Issue_Details": [ { "core_id": "CORE-000201", "message": "USUBJID is not found in DM.USUBJID", "dataset": "ae.xpt", "USUBJID": "STUDY01-009", "row": 2, "SEQ": 1, "variables": ["USUBJID"], "values": ["STUDY01-009"], } ], "Rules_Report": [ {"core_id": "CORE-000201", "status": "ISSUE REPORTED"}, {"core_id": "CORE-000351", "status": "SUCCESS"}, {"core_id": "CORE-000087", "status": "SKIPPED"}, ], } report = pb.ConformanceReport.from_core_report(core_json, agency="FDA") print(report) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ConformanceReport (CORE) Agency: FDA SDTMIG V3.4 — CORE 0.16.0 3 rules (ISSUE REPORTED=1, SKIPPED=1, SUCCESS=1) 1 issues — FAIL ``` ::: ::: The rule statuses are CORE's own. A real report would usually be read from a file, with `json.load()`. The failing record is in [`findings()`](`pointblank.ConformanceReport.findings`): ::: {#24dcf0e0 .cell execution_count=22} ``` {.python .cell-code} report.findings() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=22} ``` [CoreFinding(rule_id='CORE-000201', message='USUBJID is not found in DM.USUBJID', dataset='ae.xpt', executability=None, usubjid='STUDY01-009', row=2, seq=1, variables=['USUBJID'], values=['STUDY01-009'])] ``` ::: ::: CORE gives the row of a record as a 1-based number, so `row=2` is the second record of the AE dataset.
